Neural forecasting, uncertainty and the frozen comparison¶

This notebook trains the real N-BEATS, NHiTS, TFT, GRU, PatchTST and DLinear implementations, then compares all statistical, tabular and neural variants. Run notebook 07 first. This notebook resumes the same versioned research run.

Split conformal is a calibration method. CRPS is a scoring rule. Neither is counted as a separate trained forecasting architecture.

1. Define what the neural comparison actually tests¶

The compatible pinned implementation is NeuralForecast 1.7.7 on PyTorch 2.2.2. The six neural variants deliberately use target history only for a comparable architecture experiment. The regional arm trains a global shared-parameter univariate panel (country plus 12 regions); it is not a multivariate model of cross-region interactions. NHiTS/TFT/GRU can support covariates in separate extensions, but this notebook does not claim to test those capabilities.

Forecast 48 consecutive UTC steps from the last eligible observation, then score only tomorrow's actual 23/24/25 intervals. The training loss covers the bridge; outer selection uses delivery-day MAE. Internal early stopping uses the historical chronological tail, never outer validation or test outcomes.

Missing training labels carry mask zero. Missing predictor placeholders use causal per-series forward fill, leading zero only. Some architectures do not consume input masks directly; this imputation convention is an explicit limitation. Evaluation truth remains missing and is never interpolated.

Training-origin limitation: N-BEATS, NHiTS, TFT, PatchTST and DLinear use step_size=24 and start_padding_enabled=False. The matched panel starts at 23:00 UTC, so their training forecast blocks also begin at 23:00 UTC: 00:00 local in winter and 01:00 in summer. The replay bridge begins at 08:00 local. The library right-aligns its inner validation tail, so validation and deployment expose this mismatch rather than correcting it. GRU uses hourly recurrent windows and does not share this exact restriction. This is a limitation of the executed training policy, not a target-timestamp or inverse-scaling error. The fixed stride is visible in the hashed adapter source; it is not an explicit field in the saved trial parameters. A corrected future development run should use hourly anchors or explicitly align anchors with the cutoff and DST policy.

Architecture Development hypothesis
N-BEATS Learned trend/seasonal basis blocks capture recurring load structure.
NHiTS Multi-rate interpolation improves the direct multi-step trajectory.
TFT Temporal attention helps under the explicitly history-only input restriction.
GRU A compact recurrent representation is sufficient for demand history.
PatchTST Attention over patches improves the long-context forecast.
DLinear Simple decomposition and linear projection compete with deeper models.

DLinear is the additional neural control, not a presumed winner; its motivation is described in the original paper. The executed architectures use versioned official implementations. The cross-family leaderboard compares complete feature/model policies; it does not isolate a pure architecture effect between tabular and neural families.

2. Train and tune all six neural architectures¶

Every architecture gets two initial configurations, all four 2024 quarters and both national/global-panel arms. Notebook execution is sequential by default; the recorded execution may use bounded independent CPU workers after measured memory checks. The compact 20/40-step caps are deliberately small: they establish a reproducible baseline experiment, not an assertion that a neural family has reached its best performance. Nonfinite forecasts or training failures are retained in diagnostics; there is no substitute architecture hidden behind a model name.

Scores therefore compare these bounded feature/model/training policies. The training-origin restriction above and the history-only inputs prevent a general claim that a poorly scoring architecture is inferior to the tabular alternatives. Undertraining is plausible under these caps; it is not established as the sole cause of error.

3. Check history length, refitting, seeds and input failures¶

Development-only sensitivities compare the best national tabular model with a 365-day window, weekly refitting and full national history. These are explicitly separate from the matched-history comparison. Repeat the best validation neural candidate with all three predeclared seeds; report every result rather than selecting a lucky seed. Stress tests perturb available inputs, not outcomes. These diagnostics do not change the predeclared main monthly-refit policy.

4. Inspect neural learning curves with the correct units¶

The library's training trajectory is robust-scaled; its validation trajectory is in MW. They are plotted on separate axes. Cross-model comparison and selection use the external daily replay scores. Different seeds and quarters measure stability, not a formal bias–variance decomposition. High validation error alone does not identify overfit or underfit. Training progress at the step cap, an appropriately comparable training score, input differences and the training-origin mismatch must be considered before assigning a cause.

Development fit diagnostics¶

Saved selected-configuration forecasts from the predeclared 2024 folds only. No model was fitted and no calibration/test target values or forecast files were read.

Each fit-gap row compares the saved in-sample MAE of one fitted predictor with its raw forecasts on subsequent observations until the next fit or fold end. Fallback predictions are reported separately because they are not outputs of the same fitted predictor. Training MAE is resubstitution error and the later observations can have different regimes; this gap does not prove overfitting or provide a formal bias/variance decomposition. Models without a saved unscaled in-sample MAE have an explicitly unavailable gap; scaled neural training trajectories must not be substituted.

Quarter ranges and standard deviations describe observed seasonal/regime dispersion; quarters share overlapping training histories. They are not independent replicates or confidence intervals. Seed summaries include every recorded predeclared seed without selecting a lucky seed.

Fit groups: 368; completed model-quarter groups: 92; missing completed caches: 0; recorded seed rows: 3.

5. Freeze every candidate before final replay¶

Selection requires four validation folds and adequate raw forecast availability. Two choices have different scopes: the complete policy competes across all 23 model variants and four predeclared baselines, including RTE bias correction; the core primary is the best independent model. Both use 2024 development MAE and are frozen before final replay. The manager recommendation leads with the complete policy, so a weak independent model does not hide a stronger simple RTE-assisted policy. The historical comparison remains previously exposed; this seal cannot make it pristine again.

6. Add a genuinely fixed-predictor split-conformal comparator¶

A continuous replay fits once before January 2 calibration and retains the same fitted parameters through the final comparison. It uses only calibration errors published before the first July 1 origin. State/history updates from released observations remain permitted. This frozen comparator is distinct from the main monthly-refitted policies. Dependent, shifting demand does not establish classical exchangeability or conditional coverage guarantees.

Conformal bounds target total interval coverage. Their q05/q95 schema names do not establish equal-tailed quantiles; the center is not guaranteed to be a conditional median. No CRPS is assigned to an interval alone.

Peak-risk extension¶

The upper tail is evaluated separately during 18:00–20:00 local delivery hours. Realized temperature below 5 C defines retrospective diagnostics and scenario loss weights only. The decision trigger uses past_temperature_mean_24h below 5 C at the forecast origin; this is a past-weather proxy, not tomorrow's forecast temperature.

Pooled versus conditional empirical intervals were selected on 2024 H2, using only released 2024 H1 out-of-sample residuals. The final residual pools use January 2–June 29, 2025 outcomes released before the first test forecast. Sparse pools back off through the frozen hierarchy; counts and reasons are saved. Main point forecasts were not retuned.

The nwinters field counts represented meteorological DJF winters, not complete seasonal cycles. Inspect upper exceedance rates, severity, coverage, width and day-block confidence intervals together. A rate above 5% signals an observed upper-tail shortfall; small segments remain inconclusive. Conformal bounds do not promise equal tails or a median center. Separate hourly intervals are not simultaneous daily-peak or daily-energy intervals.

The cost table is a scenario analysis of weighted MW errors using hypothetical shortage/surplus ratios. Both the candidate and RTE empirical reference receive the same median/q95 policy and the same origin-only trigger on exactly matched observations. It is not a euro-cost model, realized financial savings, or an optimal procurement policy. A q95 choice corresponds to a 19:1 asymmetric loss only under additional distribution and decision assumptions.

7. Read point accuracy and uncertainty as different questions¶

Point table: common eligible observations, MAE/RMSE/bias/WAPE, RTE-relative gain, raw forecast availability and fallback frequency. Daily energy/peak scores exclude incomplete days explicitly. Cold-evening conditions are realized diagnostics.

Uncertainty table: native three-quantile LightGBM; empirical distributions from past out-of-sample errors; and the fixed conformal interval. CRPS is calculated exactly for the specified empirical residual distribution, not invented from a three-quantile interval. Native quantiles receive pinball and interval scores. Hourly intervals do not automatically give daily-energy or peak intervals.

Cold evenings receive their own upper-tail and interval checks. The added peak analysis freezes definitions before final scoring, evaluates counts and multi-day uncertainty, and compares a peak-conditioned residual interval chosen from development data. Cold-price multipliers and asymmetric loss ratios are sensitivity assumptions in normalized risk units, not measured euro savings. Pre-auction rules use only a pre-cutoff past-temperature proxy; realized cold conditions are diagnostic labels.

8. Defend the result and preserve its limitations¶

Block bootstrap groups paired losses into contiguous multi-day blocks; hourly errors are not treated as independent replicates. Report counts, failures, nonconvergence, uncertainty by season/hour/cold regime and computational cost.

Interpret architecture rankings only within the executed history-only neural inputs, 20/40-step caps and the five window models' training-origin mismatch. These scores support screening these configurations; they do not establish a general neural-versus-tabular result. Reported wall times also include host contention, worker suspensions and the user-requested pause recorded in execution_notes.md; they are not a clean compute-efficiency benchmark.

The recommendation addresses improvement over the supplied RTE proxy, uncertainty and failures, and the evidence still missing. This is a research project: no serving endpoint, production scheduler, procurement integration or live monitoring is created. Raw data and prediction-before-outcome ledgers are retained.

The manager report distinguishes the development-selected complete policy from the independently selected model, and uses their predeclared uncertainty methods. It preserves the original model-focused recommendation as a separate artifact.

Two frozen development choices. Across all 27 predeclared policies, the development choice is rte_bias_proxy (2024 MAE 1,029.7 MW). Across the 23 independent model variants, the core primary is gam__national (2,065.9 MW). The supplied RTE baseline has development MAE 1,428.1 MW. Both choices were frozen before test replay. The complete-policy choice uses RTE assistance and is not an independent replacement. The conformal and conditional peak analyses centered on gam__national describe that independent candidate; they do not establish uncertainty calibration for another policy. On the same locked retrospective comparison pairs, their MAEs are 1,111.0 MW for rte_bias_proxy, 1,865.7 MW for gam__national, and 1,439.0 MW for supplied RTE. The preselected complete policy's MAE improvement over RTE is 22.79%.

Manager recommendation: national day-ahead demand¶

1. Can we improve on RTE?¶

The 2024-preselected complete policy, rte_bias_proxy (RTE-assisted bias adjustment), has historical-test MAE 1,111 MW, versus 1,439 MW for the supplied RTE proxy on 8,759 matched hourly observations. Improvement: 328 MW (22.79%). Paired 14-day-block 95% intervals: relative improvement [18.99, 27.80]%; absolute improvement [266, 418] MW. The block comparison supports a historical MAE improvement.

The separate independent-model choice, gam__national, has MAE 1,866 MW. Its result does not summarize RTE-assisted attempts. Both choices were frozen using 2024 only; final-test results never choose the headline policy.

2. How uncertain, and when does it fail?¶

The complete policy uses the predeclared past-out-of-sample residual distribution. Independent-model/RTE intervals use their saved pooled/pooled choices. The independent interval decision had 33 proxy-cold observations/11 days in 2024, against the minimum 60/20. Cold evenings are 18:00, 19:00, 20:00 delivery hours with realized temperature below 5 C.

Policy Overall coverage / width MW Cold hours / days / DJF winters Cold coverage / upper misses Mean upper-miss severity MW
Complete policy 90.5% / 4,752 66 / 24 / 1 69.7% / 27.3% 1,350
Independent model 92.0% / 9,095 66 / 24 / 1 54.5% / 45.5% 2,540
RTE 91.2% / 4,896 66 / 24 / 1 71.2% / 27.3% 1,271

Intervals target 90% coverage; widths are MW. Severity is conditional on an upper-bound miss. The complete policy's cold upper-miss 14-day-block 95% interval is [12.3%, 55.3%]; status: observed upper tail exceeds nominal 5pct. DJF counts are represented winters, not full cycles; non-DJF cold events do not increase them. Sparse segments are inconclusive; zero-event bootstrap intervals [0, 0] do not prove zero risk. The 5% upper-miss target is diagnostic; conformal bounds do not guarantee equal tails. Hourly intervals are not daily-energy/maximum intervals. Scenario triggers use past-temperature proxies; realized cold is diagnostic. Statistical nonconvergence: 25/153 recorded fits; separate fit failures across all families: 0.

3. What should we use, and what are the risks?¶

Retain RTE as the operational reference and carry the preselected complete policy forward as a research candidate. Vintage archives are absent, timing/aggregation are assumed, and the 2025–26 historical test was previously inspected. Fresh prospective evidence is required.

Family rankings are confounded by 20/40-step neural caps, differing histories/features, and five windowed models' training-origin mismatch; they do not establish general architecture superiority.

Development-only regional LightGBM stress: all-history loss left 0.0% availability; missing regional inputs raised MAE 3,428→11,555 MW with 0.0% fallback. These guardrail gaps concern that tested policy.

Cold weights and shortage/surplus ratios are weighted-MW risk proxies, not euro savings or validated procurement decisions. National consumption remains a portfolio proxy.

RTE-assisted extension: matched historical comparison¶

Run notebook07's RTE-assisted development section first. This section evaluates the separately frozen16-variant tabular extension alongside the27 original policies on the same eligible origin–delivery pairs. Direct variants predict demand with RTE as a feature; residual variants learn demand minus RTE and add their output to RTE.

The 2025–26 period was previously exposed. The extension was requested after viewing earlier test results, so it is a further retrospective experiment—not a fresh confirmation set. Neither test ranking nor cold-tail outcomes select a model or trigger tuning. Original RTE issue vintages remain unavailable. National RTE is used in both data arms; no regional RTE forecast is invented.

Point forecasts and the value of RTE predictors¶

The tables retain all16 new variants, both RTE references, and each variant's original independent comparator. Scores use identical eligible observations. A negative improvement means deterioration. Separate paired7/14/28-day block resampling compares every assisted variant with raw RTE and rolling bias correction. These intervals do not eliminate selection uncertainty or turn the previously exposed test into prospective evidence.

Uncertainty and cold-evening upper-tail risk¶

Every policy receives the predeclared empirical distribution of past out-of-sample calibration errors; native LightGBM quantiles are reported separately. The development-selected assisted model also has a distinct split-conformal comparator whose fitted parameters are fixed across calibration and test. Its intervals must not be attributed to the monthly-refitted point policy. Temporal dependence means no automatic exchangeability or conditional-coverage guarantee.

Cold evenings use realized temperature<5°C at local delivery hours18/19/20 strictly for diagnosis. Counts, represented winters, upper exceedances and conditional miss severity accompany coverage and width. The upper5% diagnostic is not a guarantee, including for symmetric conformal bounds. Fixed cold weights and shortage/surplus ratios are retrospective weighted-MW risk proxies, not euro savings or actionable procurement policies. Separate hourly intervals do not define daily energy or maximum intervals.

RTE-assisted research comparison¶

1. Improvement over RTE and simple bias correction¶

The 2024-selected assisted variant is lightgbm_quantile__regional__rte_residual. The complete-policy choice across all43 alternatives was lightgbm_quantile__regional__rte_residual. These identities were frozen before new calibration/test replay. The test is previously exposed and therefore retrospective.

Policy Matched test MAE MW
Selected assisted variant 806.8
Raw RTE 1,439.0
Rolling RTE bias correction 1,111.0

On 8,759 matched hours, assisted improvement over RTE is 43.94%, or 632.2 MW; paired14-day-block95% interval [39.39, 48.31]%. Improvement over rolling bias correction is 27.39%, or 304.3 MW; interval [22.44, 30.71]%. A negative improvement means deterioration. Tables also retain every variant and its independent comparator. No winner is selected from test scores.

2. Uncertainty and cold-evening failures¶

The fixed past-out-of-sample residual distribution has nominal90% coverage, empirical overall coverage 90.5%, width 3,784 MW, and CRPS 590.7 MW. These intervals belong to the monthly-refitted policy. The separate split-conformal comparator uses one fixed fitted predictor throughout calibration/test. Native LightGBM quantiles receive quantile/interval scores, not invented CRPS. No exchangeability or conditional-coverage guarantee is established.

At realized temperature<5°C during18:00/19:00/20:00 local, there are 66 hours / 24 days / 1 represented DJF winter(s). Selected-assisted coverage is 51.5%, upper exceedance 45.5%, and conditional mean upper-miss severity 1,113 MW. Upper-exceedance14-day-block95% interval: [32.5%, 77.4%]. Status: observed_upper_tail_exceeds_nominal_5pct. The5% upper target is diagnostic; symmetric conformal intervals need not allocate equal tails. Hourly intervals do not define daily energy or maximum intervals. Interval availability and sparse segment counts remain visible. Weighted-MW shortage/cold scenarios are risk proxies, not euro savings.

3. Recommendation and limits¶

Use the executed scores to assess this research candidate against both RTE and the simple correction. A gain against raw RTE alone is insufficient evidence that learned complexity adds value. Cold-tail protection requires its separate diagnostic to pass; overall MAE does not establish it. Keep RTE as the operational reference pending authentic vintage archives and fresh prospective evidence.

There are 0 failed fit events among 817 recorded fits. Original issue versions, consumption revisions, publication delay and hourly aggregation remain unverified assumptions. Missing evaluation targets are excluded without interpolation. RTE-assisted predictions use national RTE; regional arms add regional histories, not regional RTE forecasts. The16 new variants cover four tabular families with two data arms and direct/residual targets; neural and statistical architectures were not silently altered. Searches contain two configurations and four chronological quarters. Variants are separately retuned and add both RTE and recent RTE bias, so their comparison concerns complete policies, not the isolated causal effect of one predictor. Same-fit development training/next-origin error gaps and selected quarter scores are saved; such gaps can reflect season or regime changes and are not a formal bias-variance decomposition. Zero-event bootstrap intervals do not prove zero future risk. Test results must not trigger discretionary retuning. National consumption is a portfolio proxy; no production implementation or financial-savings estimate is supplied.

Expanded RTE feature/risk evaluation¶

This section evaluates the new development-frozen candidates against raw RTE, rolling RTE bias correction and the previous studies on identical eligible origin–delivery pairs. Missing demand targets remain excluded and reported.

Separate calibration is April 2–June 29, 2025; it contains zero cold-evening observations. That is a material limitation for cold-conditional empirical and conformal coverage. The retrospective test is July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026. Earlier test outcomes may enter later scheduled fits only after release, under the frozen policy.

The native quantile model predicts q05, q075, q25, q50, q75, q90, q95 and q975. The central q05–q95 and asymmetric q075–q975 intervals both have nominal 90% mass; the latter allocates 2.5% to the upper tail. The quantile arm is selected using unweighted overall development WIS, without a cold-interval selection guardrail. It is not established as optimal for cold evenings.

Split conformal and CQR use a separate fixed engineered-only predictor, so an evolving learned-feature model is not incorrectly called fixed. That comparator still retains training weights based on out-of-sample cold probabilities while omitting those learned predictors from its inputs. Its native endpoints and calibrated bounds therefore require empirical coverage assessment; a nominal conditional-quantile interpretation is not assumed. No exchangeability or conditional-coverage guarantee is claimed.

Accuracy, risk tradeoffs and feature ablations¶

Ordinary MAE measures typical point accuracy. Cold-weighted MAE applies the declared fivefold importance scenario. Cold-segment MAE and shortage severity reveal failures that an all-hour average can hide. The selected model is chosen on development, regardless of the ordering of historical test scores.

The hybrid controls use the same historical training support and feature groups without the base-model forecast. A hybrid beating RTE does not establish that its base architecture adds value. The paired control comparison tests that narrower claim. The feature-ablation table changes feature groups and training weights under the same evaluation metric.

Distribution scores and expensive upper-tail errors¶

Pinball loss evaluates specified quantiles; WIS combines central 50% and 90% interval scores. Winkler penalizes interval width and misses. CRPS is exact here only for a fully specified past-residual empirical distribution; a few quantiles are not labelled a full distribution. Threshold-weighted CRPS emphasizes demand above a fixed pre-development threshold.

For shortage/surplus penalty ratios 1, 3, 9 and 19, the corresponding decision quantiles are q50, q75, q90 and q95. The same rule is applied to the candidate and calibrated RTE reference distributions. These are weighted-MW decision proxies, not measured euro savings. Raising the prediction is evaluated together with surplus error and interval width.

Classifier ranking metrics are undefined when a segment contains only one event class. Calibration contains one cold hour overall but no cold evening hours, so the evening cold-classifier ROC-AUC and average precision are reported as missing. This is a support limitation, not a zero performance score.

RTE-assisted feature and cold-risk research recommendation¶

Improvement over RTE¶

The development-frozen point selection is lab__lightgbm__combined__stacked__w1__residual. It passed the predeclared development guardrails. On 8,759 matched nonmissing hours, its MAE is 719.6 MW, versus 1,439.0 MW for RTE and 1,111.0 MW for rolling RTE bias correction. The RTE-relative MAE improvement is 49.99%. With cold evenings weighted five times, normalized weighted MAE is 744.7 MW; the RTE-relative improvement is 49.26%, with paired 14-day-block 95% interval [44.10, 54.28]%. Scores use exactly the same origin-delivery pairs. The earlier RTE-assisted study selected lightgbm_quantile__regional__rte_residual using development data. On these same observations it has MAE 806.8 MW and cold-evening MAE 1,611.9 MW. Relative to that prior selection, the new candidate's loss improvements are +87.1 MW overall, +33.9 MW on cold evenings, and +85.6 MW under the declared weighting (positive is improvement; negative is regression). The weighted-loss improvement's paired 14-day-block 95% interval is [+62.4, +111.4] MW. The cold-evening improvement's corresponding interval is [-219.6, +238.3] MW. Additional cold-evening point improvement over the prior policy is not established.

Uncertainty and failures¶

Cold-evening MAE is 1,578.0 MW, versus RTE's 2,427.8 MW. This segment contains 66 hours, 24 days, and 1 DJF winters. The declared chronological development selection had 102 cold-evening hours across 41 days; that limited support constrains claims about persistent winter superiority. Its past-calibration empirical 90% interval covers 43.9% of cold-evening outcomes; upper-tail misses occur in 45.5%, with 1,081 MW conditional mean severity. These are dependent historical observations, not a conditional-coverage guarantee. The separately selected native quantile model's central 90% interval covers 53.0% of cold-evening outcomes, with 37.9% upper misses. Its asymmetric 90% interval covers 59.1%, with 30.3% upper misses against a nominal 2.5% tail. The fixed engineered CQR comparator's central 90% interval covers 63.6% of cold-evening outcomes, with 30.3% upper misses. These results do not establish adequate cold-evening interval calibration. The probability tables report central and asymmetric intervals, pinball loss, central-interval WIS, upper-tail severity, and exact CRPS only for a specified empirical residual distribution. A sparse quantile grid is not labeled exact CRPS. Genuine peaks and missing-target exclusions are retained. The quantile arm was selected using unweighted overall development WIS, without a cold-interval selection guardrail; it is not established as optimal for cold evenings. The fixed engineered-only comparators retain forecast-cold training weights while omitting learned predictors from their inputs. Their native endpoints and calibrated bounds require empirical coverage assessment; nominal conditional quantiles and cold-conditional coverage are not assumed. Raw forecast availability is 99.99% and fallback frequency is 0.01%. Worst-day causes remain unproven without archived weather forecasts and input-vintage evidence.

Recommendation and risks¶

Retain the frozen point model as a candidate for the next unseen research evaluation. The interval methods do not yet support reliable cold-evening reserve-risk quantification. This is a retrospective research comparison. Use the supplied rte_forecast_d1_mw under the explicitly assumed pre-noon availability rule; no next-but-one-day product or 05:00 rule enters this experiment. The 11:00 Europe/Paris origin leaves a pre-auction buffer. Original issue vintages remain unverified. All 13 original families are represented through clearly labeled base-model-plus-RTE-feature hybrids; that does not imply native exogenous support in every neural or statistical architecture. The national, regional-history-only, and combined feature arms share national consumption as evaluation truth. Q1 2024 supplies causal stacking burn-in; the declared subsequent chronological folds select parameters and policies. Calibration runs from 2025-04-02 up to but excluding 2025-06-30. All reference methods use that same calibration period. Its seasonal and cold-support limitations are recorded in the calibration-support table. Calibration contains zero cold-evening outcomes; these uncertainty methods were not calibrated on that critical segment. The 2025–26 evaluation period was previously inspected, so prospective confirmation remains necessary. Cold weights and shortage/surplus ratios are risk scenarios in weighted MW, not euro savings. No production or procurement implementation is included. National demand remains a customer-portfolio proxy.
